content.comment_body: Hello everyone, My [product_name] 8 [article_no] is not connecting to the LAN network. I've tried various cables and switches, and I even attempted a direct connection between my laptop and the [product_name] using different cables and IP addresses, including performing a factory reset. I've observed that the LAN LED does not blink, except for a single blink when I change the IP address in the [product_name]. The diagnosis menu states the network cable is not connected. Can anyone assist?

Could you provide the IP address and subnet mask of the [product_name] as well as those of your PC? Are you able to ping the [product_name]? Start by connecting the [product_name] directly to your PC, without using any switches or routers. After a factory reset, the [product_name] typically has the IP address 192.168.0.3 and subnet mask 255.255.255.0.

Thank you for your response. The [product_name] IP address is 192.168.0.3 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. My laptop has IP address 192.168.0.10 and the same subnet mask. Even when directly connecting a cable between the [product_name] and the laptop, the diagnosis still indicates no cable is connected. Ping tests are unsuccessful.

Based on the IP addresses and subnet masks you've given, your laptop should be able to communicate with the [product_name]. However, if the diagnosis still reports that the cable is not connected and you're unable to ping the device, it strongly suggests an issue with the physical connection. Unfortunately, I cannot verify this remotely.

Please check if your [product_name] is experiencing issues with its Ethernet interface: - Disable all other Ethernet connections. - Connect your [product_name] directly to your PC using an Ethernet cable (no switch, router, or WiFi). Monitor your PC's network list; you should eventually see an active network connection that you can use to communicate with the [product_name]. Next, try pinging the [product_name]'s IP address. If successful, there could be an IP address conflict. Try changing the [product_name] IP address. You can also perform a reverse test: Disconnect the [product_name] from Ethernet and attempt to ping its IP address. If you get a response, another device in the network may have the same IP address. If the IP address is within your router's DHCP range, consider choosing one outside this range for the [product_name]. If none of these tests yield positive results, it is possible the [product_name] is faulty. Consider testing a different unit. Hope this is helpful.

Hello everyone, Thank you for all your suggestions. After contacting [company_name], they confirmed the [product_name] is defective. If the LAN LED doesn't blink when connecting to a laptop, then the LAN port is considered faulty.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have encountered a hardware failure affecting the LAN port on the [product_name] 8 module, which prevents network connectivity even after troubleshooting with multiple cables, direct connections, and resetting network configurations. The lack of LAN LED activity and a diagnostic message stating no cable is connected strongly point to a defect in the device's Ethernet interface. This hardware fault disrupts normal operations and prevents core communication between the [product_name] and a PC.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] 8 hardware to deliver reliable LAN connectivity from the start, with clear LED indications of network activity and accurate diagnostics to help identify network issues.
